turns.content: Audit prep season. The quarterly review wants a walkthrough of who can touch the archive store. Can you pull the current access list and flag anything that looks stale before I stare at it?
Pulled the archive access list and flagged three stale entries: two departed contractors and one service account from the decommissioned reporting job. Removal requests are drafted for your sign-off.

Sign-off given on all three. Next the auditors want evidence that export integrity checks actually run, not just that the code exists. Can you pull a month of verification logs into the evidence folder?
Collected the last month of export verification logs, bundled them with their checksums into the evidence folder, and added an index sheet so the auditors can sample without asking us to fish.

They also asked how long we keep the raw ingest stream versus the exported archives. The retention table in the wiki contradicts itself between two sections. Can you reconcile it against what the fleet actually does?

Reconciled the wiki retention table against the fleet's live configuration; the contradiction came from a stale copy-paste in the older section, which now matches the operative values with a note naming the source of truth.
Last prep item: the auditors want a dry-run restore from the archive picked at random. Can you schedule one for next week and make sure whoever runs it writes down the timings?

Scheduled the dry-run restore for Tuesday with a randomly picked archive day, assigned a runner from the rotation, and added a timing sheet to the evidence folder so the numbers land where the auditors will look.
